findings.title: Constructor never null-checks rawTokenId
findings.body: AccessTokenContext constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType) twice, the second with message "Null rawTokenId not allowed", and never checks rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and later encoded as the string "null" after ':' or causes NPE on decode, producing corrupt token IDs and misleading error messages.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher logic inverted and wrong offset
findings.body: The matcher splits token ID on ':' then does if (items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false. It should reject when NOT equal and grant shortcut occupies chars 4-6 (substring 4,6) of the 6-char prefix session(0-1)+token(2-3)+grant(4-5). As written any 6-char prefix with a valid UUID passes regardless of grant, so tests for authorization_code, device, refresh and ciba grants never actually verify the encoded grant and give false confidence.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut breaks custom grant providers
findings.body: Adding abstract String getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory breaks source and binary compatibility for any third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation. Existing custom grants will fail compilation and throw AbstractMethodError at runtime when loaded. It should be a default method returning a safe fallback like "na".

findings.title: Removed public copy constructor breaks compatibility
findings.body: The public Context(Context context) copy constructor was deleted. Any existing custom grant code or extension that copied grant context with new Context(oldContext) will fail compilation and throw NoSuchMethodError at runtime. It should be retained as deprecated and delegate to field copies plus grantType.

findings.title: grantType becomes stale after setFormParams and can NPE
findings.body: Context captures grantType once in the constructor from formParams.getFirst("grant_type") without null-checking formParams, then setFormParams() replaces the map without updating grantType. If formParams is null construction NPEs, and if params are replaced the encoded grant will be the stale value, causing wrong grant shortcut in the access-token ID.

findings.title: Decoding untrusted token ID throws instead of returning UNKNOWN
findings.body: getTokenContextFromTokenId returns UNKNOWN session/token/grant when there is no ':' (old UUID tokens) but throws IllegalArgumentException for wrong prefix length or unknown shortcuts. The input is the jti from a client-presented JWT, so a crafted or legacy ID containing ':' triggers an unhandled exception and 500/log spam. Handling should be consistent and return UNKNOWN for undecodable IDs.

findings.title: Lightweight detection uses context client not token client
findings.body: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext determines lightweight vs regular via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), which reads session.getContext().getClient(). TokenManager.initToken already has the correct ClientModel parameter for the token being created. If context client differs from token client or is null, the encoded tokenType is wrong and initToken can NPE, breaking token issuance on a hot path that previously never touched the context client.

findings.title: Initial offline tokens encoded as online
findings.body: Session type is derived only from userSession.isOffline() at initToken time. For an authorization-code flow requesting offline_access, the user session is still online when the access token is created and the online session is removed only afterwards in OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse. The first access token for an offline grant is therefore encoded as ONLINE while refreshed tokens are OFFLINE, defeating the stated optimization of avoiding double session lookup.

findings.title: Unknown grant aborts token creation instead of falling back
findings.body: encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException when factory.getShortcutByGrantType returns null. It is called from TokenManager.initToken for every access token. Any token whose ClientSessionContext grant attribute is set to a value without a registered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory, such as implicit/hybrid flows or custom values, will fail the whole token request with 500 instead of falling back to the existing "na" unknown-grant encoding.

findings.title: Lazy grant-map updates are non-atomic and unchecked
findings.body: getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut lazily do grantsByShortcuts.put plus grantsToShortcuts.put as two separate ConcurrentHashMap operations with no synchronization and no duplicate-shortcut validation. Concurrent first use can leave the two maps inconsistent, and a new grant reusing an existing shortcut silently overwrites the decode mapping, making future token IDs ambiguous.
